paras: A strong partnership often starts with a memorandum, which is a short document that describes what each side will do. Last year, a Brazilian support agency and an agricultural agency in Bologna signed a memorandum for a pilot with coffee and cheese producers. The Italian agency has experts who know the European market, and the Brazilian agency works with producers who have a geographic indication.

One of the key benefits is that each side gives something that the other side needs. What the Brazilian agency is offering is access to nearly five hundred certified producers. In return, the Italian agency offers its expertise in labels, export rules, and food fairs. If the pilot works, both sides will be able to leverage the results for new projects.

But a memorandum is not enough. The best partnerships have clear obligations and a clause that explains what happens if one side cannot do its part. 'Alignment is everything,' says Flavia. 'If we agree on the goals at the start, the partnership will be a win-win for the producers on both sides.'

gapfill.text: When you describe a partnership, follow three steps: what you give ('What we are offering is...'), what you want back ('In return, we would expect...'), and why it is good for both sides ('This partnership would allow us to...').

bank.label: Useful sentences to describe a partnership
items: What we are offering is access to our producers.
In return, we would expect your expertise in export rules.
This partnership would allow us to test the idea with low risk.
One of the key benefits is that both sides share the costs.
This agreement could open doors to new markets in Europe.
We work with producers who have a geographic indication.

listenings.text: Hello, Flavia. This is Giorgio, from the agency in Bologna. I read the draft of the memorandum, and I like it. I have two comments. First, the clause about the pilot is not clear. Who pays for the visits? Second, the timeline. If we sign in May, can we start the pilot in July? Our team has two experts who can work on this from July to December. Please send me a new version by Thursday. Thank you, and talk soon.

What makes a partnership strong? After twenty years of international projects, I can say three things. First, choose a partner who shares your goals. Alignment is more important than size. Second, write everything down. A clear memorandum, with obligations for both sides, prevents problems later. Third, start small. A pilot is a project that tests the idea with low risk. If the pilot works, you can grow together. In a good partnership, both sides win.

extra_audio.text: First, I describe Sebrae-SP as an institution that supports small businesses. Then, I say what we are offering. Next, I say what we would expect in return. After that, I explain one key benefit for both sides. Finally, I set one condition with if and I propose the next step.
